testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: The ____ turn on when you push the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Brake lights turn on when you push the brake pedal. An electric switch is triggered by the pedal, which turns on the lights.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems squeak too loudly.
Other braking systems are hard to find.

questions.explanation: Air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles when used and maintained properly.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a low gear and use engine braking.
Keep downshifting instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep hills, use engine braking to control your speed. Use your brakes only when needed to help slow down.

questions.question: Air tank drains should be used to:

options.text: Not be opened by the driver.
Only be opened when it is wet outside.
Remove all water and oil from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove all water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil that can damage the brakes. You must open the air tank drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Which vehicles must have emergency brakes?

options.text: Vehicles with air brakes do not need them.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have both emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving, you should:

options.text: Exit the road safely as soon as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the road safely as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning light turns on, exit the road safely and park your vehicle. Low air pressure means your brakes may not stop you safely.

questions.question: Which item is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems include an air compressor, storage tanks, drains, gauges, warning signals, and brake controls. Air filters are not part of the air brake system.

questions.question: Where are the braking mechanisms located?
questions.explanation: Brake drums are attached to the wheels on the axles. The parts that stop the vehicle are inside the brake drum.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve is releasing air, what does it mean?

options.text: This is normal and you should not worry.
There is a problem with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a problem with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve only releases air if something is wrong. Have a mechanic check and fix the problem right away.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: They are not allowed on vehicles.
They hold compressed air for the brakes.
They should be emptied after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: They hold compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold the compressed air needed to operate the brakes. The number and size of tanks varies by vehicle.

questions.question: Air tank drains should:

options.text: Only be used when it is wet outside.

questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and oil from the tanks. Always drain the tank completely.

questions.question: If brakes create too much heat:

options.text: The brakes may squeak more than usual.

questions.explanation: Brakes can fade and lose stopping power if they get too hot. Use engine braking to help slow your vehicle and avoid relying only on the brakes.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to function.
questions.explanation: Air brakes use compressed air to work.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal:

options.text: Is not required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is optional on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal. If it goes off while driving, stop and have the system repaired.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle is ____ in a minute.
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle should have a leakage rate of no more than 6 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: Why should you regularly drain the air tanks?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
To allow for a change in pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and oil that build up in the tanks and damage the brake system. Drain the tanks daily to remove these materials.

questions.question: Once the air tanks reach 125 psi, the air compressor governor will:

options.text: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
Begin pumping air into the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: When air pressure reaches about 125 psi, the governor stops the compressor. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: Failing to drain air tanks could result in:

options.text: Water freezing and causing brake failure.
Too much air collecting in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water freezing and causing brake failure.
questions.explanation: Water in the tanks can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure. Drain the tanks regularly to remove water and oil.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
It turns on the air compressor.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The governor controls the compressor. It stops pumping when pressure is too high and starts pumping when pressure is too low.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using the brake pedal can damage the brakes by putting too much force on them.

questions.question: When you need to stop suddenly in an emergency, what should you do?

options.text: Steer your trailer to the right and stop.
Steer your trailer to the left and stop.

questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, brake in a way that keeps your vehicle straight. This helps you stay safe while still allowing you to turn if needed.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use wheel chocks to stop your vehicle from rolling.
Use wheel chocks only after you set the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to stop your vehicle from rolling.
questions.explanation: When parking on a level surface, always use wheel chocks. They prevent the trailer from rolling, especially if the vehicle does not have spring brakes.

questions.question: In a static leakage test, what is the highest safe air leak rate for a double combination vehicle?
questions.explanation: The air brake system should leak no more than 3 psi in one minute. If it leaks faster, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: How far will an air brake vehicle travel before stopping at 55 mph in perfect conditions?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. At 55 mph in ideal conditions, an air brake vehicle needs about 450 feet to stop completely.
